figures.semantic_encoding: Two horizontal grouped-bar panels, one per dataset; six model rows in the original report order; raw prompts gray, T v1 masks red with white diagonal hatch. Numeric endpoint annotations. CDM NYU candidate remains NA. Independent axes explicitly labeled; no confidence intervals represented.
figures.rationale: Readers need to compare the magnitude and direction of raw-to-mask change across models; paired bars expose the large NYU changes and the near-zero HAMMER PromptDA-L change.
figures.rejected_alternative: An exact-value table is better for audit lookup, which the surrounding page can supply, but slower for recognizing the paired-change pattern. A heatmap weakens the near-equal PromptDA-L contrast.

figures.semantic_encoding: Two vertical-bar panels with three categorical variants: frozen prior, CAPA, CAPA + T v1. Frozen prior and CAPA gray; CAPA + T v1 red with white diagonal hatch. Independent axes explicitly labeled. Point estimates only; sample sizes and descriptive status printed.
figures.rationale: A small categorical comparison makes CAPA error amplification and partial recovery immediately visible while preserving the lower frozen-prior NYU error.
figures.rejected_alternative: A line chart would falsely suggest a temporal trajectory; an exact-value table would preserve values but make relative magnitudes slower to compare.
